title: Mitigation strategies and ethical use of the model

videos.script: Lesson 18 found the problem. A loyal customer in the North is flagged as a leaver more than twice as often as anybody else. The model reads a slow delivery as a fading customer. {{recap}} There are several ways to respond, and they are not equally good. You can fix what the model sees, or move the line for one group. You can change the decision itself. Or you can decide the model should not be used for it at all. {{options}} The best fix here turns out to be the cheapest: measure each customer against their own rhythm instead of everybody else's. The North's false-alarm rate falls into line, and the model loses nothing to get there. {{fix}} Then comes the part that never ends. A model that is fair in June can drift by December, and a model whose decisions change behaviour learns from its own effects. {{monitoring}} And whatever is done has to be written down. What the model is for, and what it is not for. How it does for each group, and who answers for it. {{end}}
